The paper makes a solid methodological contribution by defining saliency‑based importance scores (Equations (1)–(6) and (8)–(9)) and validating them through targeted perturbation experiments (Section 3.2 and 3.3). In particular, the authors block visual‑textual attention in the first five layers and observe a pronounced drop in accuracy (Figure 4), while blocking intra‑visual attention in deeper layers yields a larger bias (Figure 5), thereby confirming their phased‑processing hypothesis. 

Result-wise, the authors report that HiMAP reduces FLOPs from the baseline by roughly 23–24 % for the 7 B model and 23–25 % for the 13 B model (Table 1 and Table 2), while maintaining or slightly improving task accuracy across multiple-choice QA, image captioning, and open‑ended QA. Moreover, the inference speed experiments (Figures 7 and 8) demonstrate a 13–20 % acceleration compared to the FastV baseline, even allowing a 13 B model to run faster than a 7 B baseline. These metrics collectively support the claim that HiMAP offers substantial computational savings with negligible performance loss. 

The paper is clear in defining the visual‑textual versus intra‑visual flow concepts (Figure 1 and Figure 3) and discusses their implications for token pruning. However, the presentation can be dense; some figure captions lack precise descriptions, and the tables would benefit from highlighting the statistical significance of the reported improvements. 

The analysis section, while thorough conceptually, lacks statistical rigor—confidence intervals or p‑values are not reported, and the sensitivity of the pruning ratios (R₁, R₂) is only explored at a few points, limiting the robustness of the conclusions. 

Finally, the experimental setup is limited to the LLaVA‑A‑v1.5 family and a narrow set of datasets per task category. The authors do not provide a direct comparison to a no‑pruning baseline that preserves the full token set, making it difficult to isolate the effect of hierarchical pruning from other implementation details. This narrow scope may limit the generalizability of the findings to other multimodal LLM architectures.

While the paper claims novelty, the core idea of using nested prompts to subvert safety constraints is incremental relative to existing indirect jailbreak techniques.
